risk_if_not_implemented: Without Project Management Stage Gates, security, compliance and resilience requirements may be omitted from projects and initiatives until late, costly stages. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience In Project Management
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to assess security, compliance and resilience controls as part of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) project development to determine whether controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting requirements.
compensating_control_1.justification: Security, Compliance & Resilience In Project Management (PRM-08) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Project Management Stage Gates (PRM-08.1) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Security Impact Analysis for Changes
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to analyze proposed changes for potential security impacts, prior to the implementation of the change.
compensating_control_2.justification: Security Impact Analysis for Changes (CHG-06) provides risk identification and prioritization that compensates for the absence of Project Management Stage Gates (PRM-08.1) by enabling informed decisions about where to focus resources to manage residual exposure. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
